headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to pull U.S. troops out of hostilities in Niger within 30 days unless Congress approved.
what_it_does: This joint resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in, or affecting, Niger. The removal would have had to happen within 30 days after the resolution was adopted. The only exception would have been if Congress passed a declaration of war or a specific law authorizing the use of the military there. The Senate voted on October 26, 2023, not to move forward with it.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. military service members in or near Niger
who_it_affects.how: They would have been withdrawn from hostilities in or affecting Niger within 30 days unless Congress authorized their mission.

who_it_affects.group: The President and the Defense Department
who_it_affects.how: They would have been required to end U.S. military involvement in hostilities in Niger without a declaration of war or specific approval from Congress.
It would have needed to pass a declaration of war or a specific authorization for U.S. forces to keep taking part in hostilities in Niger.
